name: Fish Tank Checklist
description: A step-by-step checklist for setting up a brand-new fish tank, from equipment to adding fish.

items.text: Select a tank size suited to the fish you plan to keep
Choose a sturdy, level stand that holds the full weight
Place the tank away from direct sunlight and drafts
items.note: Sunlight encourages algae and temperature swings

items.text: Ensure a power outlet is within reach for equipment
Filter rated for the tank volume
Heater and aquarium thermometer
Lighting suited to the setup
Substrate such as gravel or sand
Water conditioner or dechlorinator
Water test kit for ammonia, nitrite, nitrate and pH
Rinse the tank, substrate and decorations with water only
Add and arrange substrate and decorations
Install and position the filter and heater
Fill with dechlorinated water and start equipment
Set the heater and let the temperature stabilize
Begin a fishless nitrogen cycle to grow beneficial bacteria
Add an ammonia source to feed the cycle
Test ammonia, nitrite and nitrate every few days
Wait until ammonia and nitrite read zero with nitrate present
items.note: This usually takes several weeks; do not rush it

items.text: Choose beginner-friendly, compatible species
Add only a few fish at first to avoid overloading the cycle
Float and slowly acclimate fish to temperature and water
Quarantine new fish if you have an established tank
Observe new fish closely for the first days
Feed small amounts and remove uneaten food
Continue testing water regularly
Perform partial water changes as needed
Watch for signs of stress or illness
Add more fish gradually once the tank stays stable

faq.q: What size fish tank is best for beginners?
faq.a: Larger tanks are generally more forgiving because water parameters stay more stable. A tank in the 20-gallon range is a common beginner choice, but always match the tank size to the fish you plan to keep.

faq.q: Do I have to cycle a new fish tank before adding fish?
faq.a: Yes. Cycling builds beneficial bacteria that convert toxic ammonia and nitrite into safer nitrate. Add fish only after the cycle is established, confirmed by testing ammonia and nitrite at zero with measurable nitrate.

faq.q: How long does it take to set up and cycle a new tank?
faq.a: Setup takes a day, but the nitrogen cycle typically takes several weeks. Test the water regularly and resist adding fish until parameters are stable — rushing is the most common cause of new-tank fish loss.

faq.q: How do I add new fish safely?
faq.a: Acclimate fish slowly to the tank's temperature and water, add only a few at a time, and avoid overstocking. For health concerns or stocking advice, consult a fish specialist or aquatic veterinarian.

faq.q: Can I print this fish tank checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can follow the setup steps in order and tick each one off.
